articles.title: Extreme heat undermines mental health, doctor warns - Türkiye Today
articles.search_term: (heatwave OR "heat wave" OR "severe heatwave" OR "extreme heat" OR "heat spell" OR "scorching heat" OR "blistering heat" OR "sweltering heat" OR "hot winds" OR loo OR "hot loo winds" OR "intense heat" OR "unbearable heat" OR "deadly heat" OR heat OR "weather forecast" OR "weather update" OR "weather alert" OR "IMD forecast" OR "IMD prediction" OR "IMD alert" OR IMD OR "rising temperatures" OR "temperatures expected to rise" OR "relief from heat" OR "respite from heat" OR "heat respite" OR "respite from scorching heat") Assam
articles.full_text:
Extreme heat affects not only physical health but also mental balance, according to Prof. Dr. Hulya Ensari, a faculty member in the Department of Mental Health and Diseases at Atlas University in Istanbul, Türkiye's largest city.
In a statement released by the university, Ensari said rising temperatures and humidity can weaken anger control, disrupt sleep quality and increase the risk of flare-ups in depression, bipolar disorder and psychotic disorders.
She added that people taking psychiatric medication should pay closer attention to fluid and electrolyte balance, as well as drug side effects, during hot weather.
A woman cools herself at a fountain during a heat wave in Italy, July 31, 2026. (AA Photo)
Heat affects mood directly
Ensari said increased arguments, shorter tempers in traffic and sudden outbursts during heat waves cannot be explained by psychological fatigue alone, since heat regulation and the regulation of emotion and sleep rely on shared mechanisms in the brain. "The impact of heat on mental state is not indirect; it is direct," she said.
She explained that when fluid and electrolyte loss, heightened alertness and disrupted sleep occur together, the brain's prefrontal functions, which are responsible for impulse control, weaken, while threat assessment becomes more dominant.
Ensari linked anger outbursts to this neurobiological imbalance, noting that the relationship between heat and aggression has been demonstrated repeatedly across different countries, periods and research methods.
She said humidity worsens the effect by blocking sweat evaporation, the body's main cooling mechanism, keeping alertness levels elevated.
Ensari also warned that hot weather can pose additional risks for people using antipsychotic, anticholinergic, antidepressant and stimulant medications, due to their effects on the body's temperature regulation and potential side effects.
Police use water cannon to cool down people in Budapest's Heroes' Square during an extreme heat wave, June 30, 2026. (AFP Photo)
No single threshold applies to everyone
She said the impact of extreme heat on mental state varies between individuals and that no single temperature is a critical threshold for everyone.
"There is no sharp threshold that applies to everyone," she said, adding that risk rises gradually with temperature rather than at a fixed point. Ensari said personal risk depends on factors including age, cardiovascular or neurological conditions, medication use, alcohol consumption, heat adaptation and humidity levels.
Sleep, she said, is a key mechanism linking heat to mental health, since falling asleep depends physiologically on heat loss through dilation of blood vessels near the skin, which lowers core body temperature.
When ambient temperature remains high, this process is disrupted, lengthening the time it takes to fall asleep and increasing nighttime waking.
A woman shields herself from the sun with a hand fan during a heat wave in Athens, Greece, July 21, 2026. (AFP Photo)
Sleep loss raises risk of manic episodes
Ensari noted that insomnia is one of the risk factors that can trigger bipolar disorder and manic episodes, and said hospital admissions related to these conditions peak during summer months, a pattern she said has been linked to high temperatures in scientific studies.

articles.title: Thunderstorm, Gusty Winds Likely in Coastal and Northern Odisha in Next 5 Days - Pragativadi
articles.search_term: ("heat advisory" OR "heat action plan" OR "heat alert" OR "IMD warning" OR "IMD alert" OR "red alert" OR "orange alert" OR "yellow alert" OR "NDMA advisory" OR "cooling shelter" OR "relief measures" OR "heat compensation" OR "severe weather warning") Assam
articles.full_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow warning for heavy rain in three districts of Odisha — Mayurbhanj, Kendujhar, and Sundaragada — as wet weather continues to grip the state.
Officials said several parts of these districts are likely to witness intense rainfall, while 11 districts including Ganjam, Gajapati, Nayagada, Khordha, Puri, and Kataka may experience thunderstorms, lightning, and gusty winds at speeds of 30–40 kmph.
The alert comes amid warnings of cyclonic rain activity across coastal and northern Odisha, with conditions expected to persist for the next five days.
Authorities have urged residents to remain cautious, particularly in low‑lying and flood‑prone areas. Farmers and fishermen have also been advised to take preventive measures against possible crop damage and rough sea conditions.
The IMD emphasised that the yellow warning is a precautionary measure, highlighting the need for preparedness as Odisha braces for another spell of heavy rain and thunderstorms.
